blocks.text: STOCKHOLM (AP) — Canadian poet, essayist and translator Anne Carson won the Nobel Prize in Literature on Thursday, October 8 for playful, genre-blending works that fuse the classical and the modern. Toronto-born Carson, 76, draws on themes and stories from ancient Greek and Roman literature. Her works often blend elements of poetry, essay, and fiction. Ingrid Carlberg, permanent secretary of the Swedish Academy, said that the author was in Iceland “listening to the wind” when the academy reached her. “She was very taken by surprise,” Carlberg said.
